mechanism: Deribit lists the dominant BTC/ETH options open interest and settles weekly and monthly contracts every Friday 08:00 UTC. In the ~24h run-up to settlement, option dealers who are net short gamma near busy strikes must delta-hedge by buying into dips and selling into rallies to stay flat, which mechanically compresses realized moves and pulls spot toward the strike concentration ("pinning"); once the position expires and gamma resets, the pinning force disappears. The forced counterparty is the option-selling dealer desk, which is contractually obligated to re-hedge delta continuously regardless of price view -- that hedging flow is what a fade-the-extension strategy harvests.
counterparty: Deribit BTC/ETH option market-maker desks that are short gamma near expiry and must mechanically buy dips / sell rallies to stay delta-neutral into the Friday 08:00 UTC settlement -- their hedging flow suppresses/reverts extensions, which is what this thesis fades.
prediction: In the 24h window before Friday 08:00 UTC Deribit settlement, BTC and ETH 1h closes that deviate >1% from the trailing 5-day (120h) SMA revert toward that SMA by the time of/shortly after settlement, at a rate that clears p*(150bps)=53.83% (research/swarm/runs/2026-09-20-0300/mandate.md section 3) net of the 11.5bps round-trip cost.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 7 killed generic time-of-day/CME-gap/weekend/Saturday calendar noise -- session liquidity patterns with no forced counterparty. This thesis's mechanism is option-dealer delta-hedging under short gamma into a specific, published settlement instant (Deribit 08:00 UTC Friday), not ambient session timing; the counterparty is a hedging desk with a contractual obligation, not generic liquidity thinness.

Row 20 (funding-spike carry) is a funding-rate arbitrage mechanism (linear perp funding vs. spot/basis), armed but never deployed. This thesis has nothing to do with funding payments; it trades options-dealer gamma hedging on the underlying spot/perp price, an entirely different derivative and forced-flow source.

Row 76 (multi-day MR / overnight window / vol-scaling) was refuted as a generic multi-day mean-reversion premium, dead post-2022 and web-verified dead. This thesis is not an unconditional MR premium -- it is gated to a specific externally-documented options-expiry window with a named counterparty (option dealer gamma hedging), which is the distinction STANDARDS #1 requires.

evidence: ScienceDirect (2026), 'Bitcoin option expiration, gamma exposure, and intraday price reversals': documents a statistically and economically significant return reversal around Deribit BTC option expiration, concentrated on days with elevated at-the-money open interest and strongest when cumulative gamma exposure is negative -- consistent with option market makers hedging net-short gamma exposure -- with an estimated economic significance of about USD 50 million/year in wealth transfer from the expiration effect. MenthorQ's dealer-flow guide (2026) corroborates the mechanism qualitatively: when dealers run net short gamma, hedging reinforces moves into the pin and that pressure reverses once gamma resets post-expiry. I could not access exact effect-size percentages from the paywalled ScienceDirect abstract page (403 on WebFetch); the $50M/yr figure and the negative-gamma/reversal finding are the numbers actually reported in the fetched search summary of that page.
